passage:
Varun stood at the courtyard door. "Rafiq! Lunch, beta!"
The toddler did not look up. He tipped the red cup and sand hissed into the blue one.
"Rafiq, roti!" Nothing. Blue cup, red cup, and back again.
Varun crouched beside his son. "Two more pours, then we eat, okay?" Rafiq poured once, twice, and let Papa lift him. His lip shook, and a small wail began as the cups stayed behind.

qa.q: What did Rafiq pour from one cup to the other?
qa.a: Sand, tipped from the red cup into the blue one.

qa.q: What was Rafiq feeling when Papa lifted him away from the cups?
qa.a: He felt upset and sad. His lip shook and a wail began because his pouring had been cut off.

qa.q: What could Varun try next time to make stopping easier?
qa.a: He could give a short warning like 'two more pours' a little earlier, and help Rafiq set the cups aside so they are waiting after lunch. 🙂

qa.q: What might Varun understand about Rafiq's crying after this?
qa.a: That it is not naughtiness. Rafiq was so absorbed that being lifted away felt like losing something, so a gentle warning would help.

grounding: A toddler is absorbed in pouring sand and cries when pulled away from it.

passage:
Note, Tuesday. Lavanya, two years old, spent the morning at the sand tray pouring from a yellow cup into a green one, again and again. She ignored the lunch bell and my calls. When I lifted her she cried hard and reached back for the tray.
Wednesday. I sat beside her before lunch, said, "The cups are going to sleep soon," and helped her shelve them. She frowned but walked to the table holding my hand.
Maria, key worker

qa.q: Which two cups did Lavanya pour between at the sand tray?
qa.a: She poured from a yellow cup into a green one.

qa.q: How did Lavanya feel when Maria lifted her away on Tuesday?
qa.a: She felt distressed. She cried hard and reached back for the tray, which shows how much the pouring mattered to her.

qa.q: What changed in what Maria did on Wednesday?
qa.a: Maria gave a warning first, said the cups were going to sleep, and helped shelve them, so the stop felt gentler.

qa.q: What would Lavanya's Tuesday have felt like if the cups had had a place to wait?
qa.a: She might still have been sad to stop, but she would know the cups were safe, so leaving them would hurt less.

grounding: A toddler absorbed in pouring cries when pulled away abruptly, and a caregiver softens the transition.

passage:
Monday. Aditi squatted in the park sandpit, pouring sand from a red cup into a blue one, again and again. Her papa, Mohit, called "Lunch!" three times. She didn't look up. When he lifted her away, she wailed all the way home.
Wednesday. Mohit crouched beside her. "Two more pours, then lunch." She poured twice and looked at him.
Friday. Aditi poured, then held the cup out to Papa herself and toddled to the bench.

qa.q: What colours were Aditi's cups?
qa.a: A red cup and a blue one.

qa.q: Why did Aditi wail when Mohit lifted her away?
qa.a: She was upset at being pulled out suddenly from the pouring she was completely lost in.

qa.q: What worked better on Wednesday?
qa.a: Mohit crouched beside her and warned, "Two more pours, then lunch," so she could finish on her own.

qa.q: How might Mohit feel on Friday when Aditi hands him the cup?
qa.a: Mohit likely feels relieved and pleased that lunch came without tears.

grounding: Shows a toddler absorbed in pouring sand, crying when pulled away abruptly, and settling when given a small warning.

passage: On the balcony of their Chennai flat, two-year-old Sangeeta sat by a tub of river sand, tipping a steel tumbler into a small katori. Pour, tap, pour. Her grandmother called, "Sangeeta, rice is ready!" Nothing. Her big brother Yogesh, hungry and impatient, grabbed the tumbler. "Come on!" Sangeeta's face crumpled and she howled, fists tight. Paati took the tumbler back, gave it to her, and sat down with the rice plate right there on the balcony.

qa.q: What was Sangeeta pouring the sand into?
qa.a: A small katori.

qa.q: Why did Sangeeta howl when Yogesh grabbed the tumbler?
qa.a: She was upset and frustrated at having her pouring snatched away so suddenly.

qa.q: What did Paati do that helped?
qa.a: Paati gave the tumbler back and brought the rice to the balcony, so lunch came without a fight.

qa.q: Why might Yogesh have grabbed the tumbler?
qa.a: Yogesh was hungry and impatient, and probably didn't see how absorbed his little sister was.

grounding: Shows a toddler deep in pouring sand who does not hear the lunch call and cries when the cup is snatched.

passage:
"Pema, lunch time!" Jaya called across the creche.
"She hasn't heard you," said Asha, the helper. "Look at her."
In the sand corner Pema was scooping with a yellow cup and tipping it into a green one, watching the grains slide. Scoop, tip. Scoop, tip.
"Twenty minutes she's been at that," Jaya said softly.
"Should I carry her?"
"Last time we did that she cried till nap. Let me try." Jaya knelt. "Pema, one more cup, then dal."
Pema tipped one more cup, then held up her arms.

qa.q: How long had Pema been pouring, according to Jaya?
qa.a: Twenty minutes.

qa.q: What does Pema not hearing the call suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Pema is completely absorbed and content in the scooping and tipping.

qa.q: Why did Jaya kneel instead of carrying Pema?
qa.a: Carrying her last time led to crying till nap, so Jaya gave a small warning, one more cup, and let Pema finish.

qa.q: How does Asha see Pema's pouring?
qa.a: Asha notices how deeply Pema is focused, pointing out she hasn't heard and inviting Jaya to look.

grounding: Shows a toddler so absorbed in pouring sand that she misses the lunch call, and a caregiver ending it gently.

passage:
Playgroup note, Thursday
Nilesh spent nearly half an hour at the sand tray, pouring sand from a red cup into a blue cup and back, humming. When Divyansh called him, he didn't look up. When I said "Lunch time!" twice, he didn't hear.
I lifted him away too quickly, and he burst into tears and reached back for the cups.
Next time I will kneel beside him first, pour once with him, then say "Last pour, then lunch." 🙂

qa.q: What colours were Nilesh's cups?
qa.a: Nilesh poured sand from a red cup into a blue cup and back.

qa.q: Why did Nilesh burst into tears when he was lifted away?
qa.a: Nilesh felt upset and frustrated at being pulled suddenly out of an absorbing game he was enjoying.

qa.q: What small change does the caregiver plan for next time?
qa.a: To kneel beside him, pour once with him, and give a gentle "last pour" warning before lunch.

qa.q: How might Divyansh have felt when Nilesh didn't look up?
qa.a: Divyansh might have felt a little ignored or puzzled, not knowing Nilesh was too absorbed to hear.

grounding: A caregiver's note shows a toddler absorbed in pouring sand, deaf to lunch calls, and tearful when pulled out abruptly.
